sources.note: Builds multi-layer steering vectors from SAE features selected by co-activation and decoder-direction alignment, and intervenes at several points instead of one.
sources.title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits

sources.note: Reverse-engineers the arithmetic circuit down to individual neurons and finds it is neither a learned algorithm nor memorization, but an unordered collection of sparse heuristic neurons that each fire on a numerical input pattern and vote for corresponding answers.
sources.title: Arithmetic Without Algorithms: Language Models Solve Math With a Bag of Heuristics

sources.note: Uses causal mediation analysis on a minimal propositional logic task to recover a sparse reasoning circuit in Mistral-7B and Gemma-2 up to 27B, and decomposes it into four families of attention heads that execute rule locating, rule moving, fact processing and decision making as sequential steps.
sources.title: A Implies B: Circuit Analysis in LLMs for Propositional Logical Reasoning

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'circuit discovery'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.

result.definition: Finding the subgraph of components responsible for a behaviour, and across 3 sources a method whose results in this archive divide by whether a circuit is found at all. It is found for propositional logic: four families of attention heads executing rule locating, rule moving, fact processing and decision making as sequential steps, recovered by causal mediation across models from 7B to 27B. It is not found for arithmetic: the circuit reverse-engineered to individual neurons is neither a learned algorithm nor memorisation but an unordered collection of sparse heuristic neurons each firing on a numerical input pattern and voting for corresponding answers. And one source builds on discovered circuits rather than discovering them, using sparse-autoencoder circuits to align steering across layers geometrically. The archive's caution for all three is the identifiability one: where the units come from a learned dictionary rather than from the weights, the circuit is partly a property of the dictionary.
